title: Apple warns tariffs could raise iPhone costs by $900M next quarter
text: Apple warned investors that newly announced US tariffs on imported electronics could add roughly $900 million to its costs next quarter. The company said it is accelerating supply chain diversification but expects margin pressure through year end. Shares fell on the news as analysts cut earnings estimates.

title: Nvidia beats earnings as AI data center demand surges
text: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue well above Wall Street expectations, driven by surging demand for AI data center chips. Management raised full-year guidance and announced a new share buyback. The stock jumped in after-hours trading on the strong results.

title: Fed holds rates steady, signals caution on inflation
text: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady and signaled it remains cautious about persistent inflation. Chair comments suggested rate cuts are unlikely before mid-2027, pressuring growth stocks including Microsoft and Alphabet as treasury yields climbed.

title: Microsoft closes $4B acquisition of AI startup DeepForge
text: Microsoft announced it has closed its $4 billion acquisition of AI infrastructure startup DeepForge, the largest deal of the year in enterprise software. The acquisition deepens Microsoft's AI moat and is expected to be accretive within two years.

title: Exxon Mobil downgraded as crude outlook weakens
text: A major rating agency downgraded Exxon Mobil's credit outlook to negative, citing weakening crude prices and rising capital expenditure. The downgrade triggered a selloff in energy bonds and raised default hedging costs across the sector.

title: Tesla launches robotaxi service in Austin
text: Tesla officially launched its robotaxi service in Austin with a fleet of 200 autonomous vehicles. Early rider reviews are positive and the company plans expansion to three more cities next quarter. Shares rallied on the product launch milestone.

title: JPMorgan warns of rising credit defaults in commercial real estate
text: JPMorgan's chief risk officer warned that commercial real estate loan defaults are rising faster than expected, forcing the bank to raise loss provisions. The warning dragged financial stocks lower and widened credit spreads.

title: Amazon unveils AI shopping assistant ahead of holiday season
text: Amazon unveiled a new AI-powered shopping assistant integrated across its app and Echo devices ahead of the holiday season. Analysts say the product launch could lift conversion rates and boost fourth-quarter retail revenue.

title: China retaliates with rare earth export curbs
text: China announced retaliatory export curbs on rare earth minerals in response to Western chip sanctions, escalating the trade war. Apple and Broadcom suppliers warned of potential shortages, and technology shares fell across Asia and Europe.

title: UnitedHealth cuts guidance as medical costs surge
text: UnitedHealth cut its full-year earnings guidance after medical costs surged beyond expectations. The announcement triggered a broad healthcare selloff and raised fears of a credit rating downgrade for the insurer.

title: Meta acquires VR studio in $1.2B metaverse bet
text: Meta Platforms announced the $1.2 billion acquisition of a leading VR game studio, deepening its metaverse bet. The deal follows the successful launch of its new Quest headset and was welcomed by investors.

title: Recession fears grow as unemployment ticks up
text: Fresh labor data showed unemployment ticking up for a third straight month, reviving recession fears. Economists at JPMorgan raised recession odds, and consumer discretionary stocks including Home Depot and Amazon fell on weakening demand expectations.

title: Visa launches instant settlement for merchants
text: Visa launched a new instant settlement product allowing merchants to access funds within minutes. The product launch strengthens Visa's competitive position against Mastercard in the payments race and was praised by analysts.

title: Broadcom bids $8B for software maker in takeover push
text: Broadcom submitted an $8 billion takeover bid for an enterprise software maker, continuing its acquisition spree. The merger would expand Broadcom's software revenue mix, though regulators are expected to scrutinize the deal.

title: Oil spikes as Middle East conflict escalates
text: Crude oil prices spiked 6% as conflict in the Middle East escalated, raising geopolitical risk premiums. Exxon Mobil shares surged on higher price realizations while airlines and consumer stocks fell on fuel cost fears.

title: Google debuts Pixel with on-device Gemini AI
text: Google debuted its new Pixel phone with on-device Gemini AI features at its annual hardware event. The product launch drew strong reviews and preorders beat internal targets, lifting Alphabet shares.

title: Procter & Gamble spins off beauty division
text: Procter & Gamble announced plans to spin off its beauty division into a standalone company, the biggest portfolio shakeup in a decade. The divestiture is expected to unlock shareholder value and sharpen focus on core consumer staples.

title: Mastercard hit by downgrade wave across payments sector
text: Analysts downgraded several payments companies including Mastercard, citing slowing cross-border volumes and rising credit risk. The credit event repricing sent financial stocks lower for a second straight session.

title: Nvidia faces fresh US export ban on AI chips to China
text: Washington is weighing fresh export bans on advanced AI chips sold to China, directly threatening Nvidia's second-largest market. The geopolitical escalation could wipe billions from Nvidia's revenue and reshapes the global chip trade.

title: Home Depot warns housing slowdown to hit sales
text: Home Depot warned that the housing slowdown and high interest rates will weigh on sales through next year. The macroeconomic headwinds prompted the retailer to cut its outlook, sending shares lower.
